properties.decision: Not decided. Recorded as brainstorming, not as a proposal.
properties.name: OPEN — what should `accepted` mean on an evidence record, if anything, given that evidence "is never read as a requirement awaiting the owner's acceptance"?
properties.rationale:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From the public legal-case trial's F9 (2026-10-25): the agent set `status: accepted` on evidence records. Each was signed as the account owner (via the agent), and the agent itself asked what `accepted` means for evidence.

The accepted requirement req:evidence-carries-its-source-grade-and-confidence-and-is-not-intent says evidence is never read as intent awaiting acceptance. Yet the status field is still writable on it.

Options:
(a) `accepted` on evidence means "admitted": the owner agrees it is in the record. It is read back, and changes no truth.
(b) Status is refused on evidence, with a refusal that says why.
(c) Leave it as is and say in the skill not to set it.

COUNTER-ARGUMENT: (b) removes a field some designs may already use. Count them first. Related setup finding: hub fact:a-role-played-trial-signs-approvals-as-the-owner-with-the-agent-recorded-only-as-via-2026-10-25.
